text:
===== FILE 20220__1.pdf =====
September 2, 2025 
Re: Docket VA-2025-VHA-0073-0002 
Thank you for the opportunity to comment on the Department of Veterans Affairs’ (VA) proposal to fully exclude 
abortions and abortion counseling from the medical beneﬁts package provided to veterans and their families—even 
in cases of rape, incest, or health emergencies. This dangerous policy would block care for millions who access 
health care through the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and would only permit a narrow exception to save 
the life of a pregnant veteran.  The proposed change in the medical beneﬁts package goes against the VA’s core 
values of integrity, commitment, advocacy, respect, and excellence (ICARE) and its mission to provide exceptional 
health care services to improve the health and well-being of Veterans and their families.  
Access to abortion care is crucial for veterans to maintain their health, dignity, and autonomy, particularly given the 
high rates of military sexual trauma and the restrictive abortion laws in many states where veterans live. Without 
such access  veterans face ﬁnancial burdens and potential health crises, as they are forced to navigate complex 
logistical and economic barriers to receive necessary care. Providing abortion services within the VA ensures that 
veterans receive comprehensive reproductive healthcare, akin to the services available to other civilians, and 
upholds the government's promise to care for them after their service.  
Access to abortion is essential for patient safety, bodily autonomy, economic well-being, and health outcomes, as 
restricting it leads to increased risks from unsafe abortions and complicated pregnancies, higher rates of maternal 
mortality, and lasting economic hardship. Access allows individuals to make informed decisions about their health 
and futures, improves women's labor force participation and educational attainment, and is a component of 
comprehensive healthcare necessary for overall public health.  
More than 9 million veterans receive their health care from the VA, and women veterans of reproductive age between 
ages 18-44 are also the fastest growing subset of new VA users. Notably, more than 400,000 women veterans live in 
states that severely restrict or ban abortion.   The proposed VA policy will  undoubtedly endanger the health and lives 
of millions of veterans across the country and leave them without the essential health care and support they need 
and deserve.  
The Illinois Public Health Association (IPHA) is one of the largest affiliates of the American Public Health Association 
and is widely recognized as a leader in the ﬁeld of public health advocacy, health education, and promotion.  IPHA 
and its members have a strong commitment to ensuring access to healthcare for all populations.  Veterans have 
historically faced signiﬁcant barriers to reproductive health care, and with the current patchwork of abortion bans 
and restrictions across the country, these barriers are even steeper today.  The Illinois Public Health Association 
urges the federal Veteran’s Administration to support veterans and their families by providing access to abortion 
care and counseling as currently provided for under the  VA and CHAMPVA medical beneﬁts package. 
Sincerely,  
 
Tom Hughes 
Executive Director 
Illinois Public Health Association
